You can make your doctags document iterable by pages using the `<page_break>` tag. The recommended approach is to split your doctags string on `<page_break>`, which gives you a list where each element represents a page. For example, in Python:

```python
pages = doctags_string.split("<page_break>")
```

If you want a more structured solution, the `DocTagsDocument` class in `docling-core` (located in `docling_core/types/doc/document.py`) provides a `pages` attribute—a list of page objects—when you construct it using `from_multipage_doctags_and_images`. This method automatically splits the doctags string by page breaks and organizes the content per page, making iteration straightforward. The `docling-core` library is part of the Docling project, which is an open-source document processing library that converts documents (PDFs, DOCX, etc.) into structured formats and extracts text, tables, and other elements.

Both methods work: string splitting is quick and simple, while the class-based approach gives you more structure if you need to work with page metadata or images.
